title: Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026: Win Up to $8,000 by Building Offline AI That Runs on Everyday Laptops Across Africa.
summary: Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries worldwide, but one of the biggest barriers preventing widespread AI adoption across Africa is the high cost of cloud computing, expensive infrastructure, unstable internet connectivity, and unreliable electricity. To address these challenges, the Africa Deep Tech Foundation (ADTF) has officially launched the Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 – The Laptop LLM Challenge , a groundbreaking competition designed to encourage innovators to develop AI systems that run efficiently on affordable laptops already available across the continent. Rather than rewarding teams for building the largest language models, ADTC 2026 focuses on creating practical, efficient, and locally deployable AI applications capable of running entirely offline. Participants are invited to demonstrate that cutting-edge AI can be accessible, affordable, and useful for millions of people without requiring expensive cloud services or powerful GPUs. With a total prize pool of $20,000 , mentorship opportunities, venture support, GPU credits, and recognition from Africa s growing deep technology ecosystem, this challenge provides an excellent opportunity for AI developers, researchers, startups, and students to showcase innovative solutions that solve real-world African problems. Application Deadline: August 25, 2026 (Gate 1 Submission) What is the Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026? The Africa Deep Tech Challenge (ADTC) 2026 is an applied systems engineering competition organized by the Africa Deep Tech Foundation. Unlike traditional AI competitions that emphasize larger models or cloud-hosted systems, this challenge focuses on building practical AI applications capable of operating entirely on consumer-grade laptops commonly used throughout Africa. The challenge encourages participants to optimize language models so they deliver strong performance while operating under strict hardware limitations. The objective is to democratize access to AI by ensuring advanced language models can function efficiently even where internet connectivity and computational resources are limited. The competition emphasizes engineering excellence in areas such as: Model quantization Memory optimization Efficient compilation Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Offline knowledge systems Fast inference Responsive user experience Local data integration The broader vision is to develop AI that people across Africa can own, run, and trust without depending on expensive cloud infrastructure. Why This Challenge Matters Across many African countries, accessing cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) remains expensive due to API costs, internet requirements, and inconsistent electricity. The Africa Deep Tech Foundation believes the solution is not simply creating larger AI models but engineering smarter systems capable of operating on hardware that millions of Africans already own. The competition highlights several important challenges: Limited Access to Cloud AI Many users cannot rely on continuous internet access or afford subscription-based AI services. Examples include: University students Healthcare facilities Small businesses Farmers Community organizations Local entrepreneurs Offline AI significantly reduces these barriers. AI for Affordable Hardware Instead of requiring expensive GPUs, the challenge targets affordable laptops costing between $150 and $500 , making AI deployment far more accessible. Efficient AI Engineering Participants are expected to optimize every aspect of model performance, including: RAM usage Processing speed User experience Memory allocation Model compression Local retrieval systems Competition Problem Domains Participants must choose one primary application area while demonstrating at least one meaningful cross-disciplinary integration. Available domains include: 1. Mathematics and Scientific Reasoning Possible applications include: Mathematical problem solving Proof assistance Scientific calculations Quantitative reasoning 2. Healthcare and Medical Support Potential solutions include: Clinical question answering Patient education Healthcare information Medical triage assistance 3. Agriculture Innovators can develop AI tools that support: Crop management Livestock advisory Weather information Agricultural planning Market intelligence 4. Creative Writing Possible applications include: Story generation Editing assistance Poetry Multilingual writing Content creation 5. Coding Assistants Developers may create offline tools capable of: Code generation Debugging Programming tutorials Software development assistance 6. Enterprise Productivity Business-focused applications may include: Knowledge management Internal documentation SME productivity Workflow support 7. Autonomous AI Agents Participants can develop intelligent offline agents capable of: Workflow automation Privacy-focused task execution Local orchestration Offline decision support REGISTER HERE Hardware Requirements Every submission must successfully operate on the official ADTC Standard Laptop. Target hardware specifications include: Component Requirement CPU Intel Core i5 (10th–12th Generation x86-64) RAM 8 GB DDR4 Maximum Memory Usage 7 GB Graphics Intel UHD or Iris Xe Integrated Graphics Storage 256 GB SSD Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS GPU No discrete GPU allowed Any submission exceeding the 7 GB RAM limit during evaluation will be immediately disqualified. African Language Bonus Projects demonstrating meaningful support for at least one African language receive an additional 15% panel score bonus . This encourages participants to develop AI systems that better reflect Africa s linguistic diversity while improving accessibility for local communities. Competition Timeline The competition consists of three evaluation stages. Gate 1 – Submission Package Deadline: August 25, 2026 Participants must submit: Open-source GitHub repository Structured REPORT.md Screenshots or demonstration clips Two-minute demonstration video Bonus documentation (African language support or budget laptop testing) Gate 2 – Activities and Technical Audit Dates: September 8 – September 29, 2026 Selected teams will participate in: 30-minute technical Q A Reproducibility audit Reviewer clarification Optional benchmark updates Optional feedback responses Gate 3 – Final Package Deadline: October 17, 2026 Finalists must prepare: Maximum 10-slide pitch deck Live presentation attendance Technical setup verification Scoring Criteria Every submission undergoes standardized benchmarking using the official ADTC hardware profile. Accuracy – 50% Judges evaluate: Automated benchmark performance Prompt quality Model correctness Overall reasoning ability Speed – 30% Measured according to token generation speed relative to the fastest submission. Efficiency – 20% Rewards lower RAM usage during execution. Lower memory consumption results in higher efficiency scores. Additional Rules Thermal Penalty Teams lose 10 points if: CPU temperature exceeds 85°C Thermal throttling occurs Automatic Disqualification Submissions are immediately disqualified if: The application crashes Out-of-memory errors occur RAM exceeds 7 GB Performance Bonuses Participants can further improve their scores through: Budget Hardware Profile Bonus (+10%) African Language Bonus (+15%) Local Benchmarking Tool To help participants prepare for official evaluation, ADTF provides an open-source local profiling tool that measures: CPU utilization Memory usage Latency Throughput Overall hardware compatibility This enables teams to optimize performance before submission. Prize Pool The competition offers a total prize pool of $20,000 , along with additional technical and ecosystem support. Grand Prize The winning team receives: $8,000 cash Six-month scale-up residency Venture Demo Day participation Pilot matchmaking ADTC Certified Trust-Mark Governance and legal mentorship Product hardening mentorship Runner-Up Prize includes: $4,000 cash Three-month residency Pilot matchmaking Venture Demo Day access Best Integration Award Awarded to the strongest cross-disciplinary solution. Prize: $3,000 cash Best Localisation Award Recognizes outstanding African language or local context integration. Prize: $1,500 cash GPU Credits Finalists $250 GPU cloud credits Up to ten finalists Semi-finalists $50 GPU cloud credits Up to twenty semi-finalists Ecosystem Partners The competition is supported by a growing ecosystem of organizations dedicated to strengthening Africa s deep technology landscape. Partners include organizations across: AI research Venture development Technology communities Innovation hubs Open-source communities Developer networks Frequently Asked Topics Participants can expect guidance on topics such as: Offline model evaluation Hardware benchmarking African language eligibility Cross-disciplinary integration Open-source model usage Quantization tools Deployment frameworks Model size limitations Accuracy benchmarks Thermal monitoring Hybrid versus offline architectures Video demonstration requirements How to Participate Entering the challenge involves three simple steps: Step 1 Register your project through the official submission platform. Step 2 Work individually or build a team of up to three members. Step 3 Read the competition rules, use the submission template, benchmark your model locally, and submit your complete Gate 1 package before the deadline. Important Dates at a Glance Gate 1 Submission Deadline: August 25, 2026 Technical Audit: September 8 – September 29, 2026 Final Package Deadline: October 17, 2026 To learn more about the opportunity Visit HERE. Conclusion The Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026 represents an ambitious effort to redefine how artificial intelligence is developed and deployed across Africa. By focusing on lightweight, offline-capable AI systems that run on affordable consumer laptops, the competition seeks to remove barriers associated with cloud computing, internet dependence, and expensive hardware. Beyond the attractive cash prizes, participants gain access to mentorship, technical validation, investor exposure, venture support, and recognition within Africa s rapidly expanding deep technology ecosystem. Whether you are an AI researcher, software engineer, startup founder, student, or independent innovator, this challenge provides an opportunity to contribute practical AI solutions designed specifically for the realities of African communities. If you are passionate about building accessible, efficient, and impactful artificial intelligence, now is the time to begin developing your solution. Be sure to prepare your open-source project, optimize it for the official hardware requirements, and submit your Gate 1 entry before August 25, 2026 For more OFY Competition opportunities Click HERE . title: UNESCO Doctoral Internships 2026–2027 in Paris, France | Fully Supported Research Internship for UCL PhD Students
summary: The UNESCO Doctoral Internships 2026–2027 present an outstanding opportunity for doctoral researchers at University College London (UCL) to gain international research experience while contributing to one of UNESCO s flagship education initiatives. Hosted at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris , these six-month research internships will allow successful applicants to work directly with the Global Happy Schools Initiative , a UNESCO-led programme dedicated to promoting educational equity, wellbeing, peace, inclusion, and values-based education around the world. Developed through the partnership between UNESCO s Happy Schools Initiative and UCL s Grand Challenge of Inequalities , the internships provide doctoral students with the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research addressing some of today s most pressing educational challenges, including peacebuilding, community learning, social cohesion, displacement, and educational inequalities. Successful interns will receive financial support toward accommodation in Paris and travel between London and Paris, making this a valuable opportunity for doctoral students interested in international education, public policy, educational research, and sustainable development. About the UNESCO Doctoral Internship Programme UNESCO is inviting applications from doctoral students currently enrolled at University College London (UCL) to participate in one of two research internships focused on advancing the Global Happy Schools Initiative . The internships are designed to explore how education systems can create learning environments that foster: Educational equity Student and teacher wellbeing Peacebuilding Social cohesion Community engagement Democratic participation Inclusive education Lifelong learning Interns will be based at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris , where they will work alongside experts involved in implementing and expanding the Global Happy Schools Initiative. The placements are expected to begin no later than March 2027 and will run for six months . What is the UNESCO Global Happy Schools Initiative? The Global Happy Schools Initiative is a UNESCO-led programme that promotes educational environments where wellbeing, equity, inclusion, and values-based learning become central components of school systems. Rather than measuring success solely through academic performance, the initiative recognizes that thriving schools are built through positive relationships, supportive learning environments, inclusive practices, and community participation. The initiative seeks to improve both wellbeing and educational outcomes by creating schools where learners, educators, and communities can flourish together. The Four Pillars of the Happy Schools Framework At the heart of the initiative is the Happy Schools Framework , which organizes positive learning environments around four interconnected pillars. 1. People This pillar focuses on: Positive relationships Emotional wellbeing Social-emotional learning Respect Positive attitudes Strong teacher-student relationships Research demonstrates that healthy interpersonal relationships contribute significantly to improved learning outcomes and student wellbeing. 2. Process This pillar emphasizes: Balanced curricula Active learning Innovative teaching approaches Holistic assessment methods Student-centered pedagogies Rather than relying solely on examinations, the framework promotes learning experiences that encourage participation, creativity, and critical thinking. 3. Place The Place pillar focuses on creating supportive learning environments through: Inclusive schools Safe physical spaces Accessible digital learning Community-centered education Welcoming school environments These environments encourage collaboration, inclusion, and lifelong learning. 4. Principles The Principles pillar promotes: Trust Inclusion Empowerment Democratic participation Equity Shared values Together, these principles create school cultures where every learner feels valued and supported. Countries Already Participating The Happy Schools Initiative has already been launched in several countries, including: Portugal Viet Nam Japan Lao People s Democratic Republic Thailand The initiative continues to expand internationally as UNESCO works with governments and education partners worldwide. Internship Duration The selected interns will complete: Six-month research placement Based at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris Expected to begin no later than March 2027 Financial Support Successful applicants will receive financial assistance from UCL, including: Contribution toward accommodation costs in Paris Support for travel between London and Paris This funding helps reduce the financial burden associated with undertaking an international research placement. Visa Support As the internships will take place in France, successful applicants will receive visa guidance from the French Embassy . Participants will be required to apply for a French student trainee visa through the French Consulate because they will not be enrolled in a French higher education institution during the internship. The Embassy will provide: Information on visa requirements Guidance throughout the application process Support regarding relevant French visa procedures Internship Opportunity 1: Pedagogies for Peace and the Happy Schools Initiative The first internship focuses on understanding how the Happy Schools Framework can be expanded into settings affected by: Armed conflict Forced displacement Social inequality Fragile communities Economic disadvantage The research seeks to explore how schools can become spaces that actively promote: Peacebuilding Democratic participation Social cohesion Inclusive education Conflict-sensitive teaching This internship investigates how educational environments can contribute to peaceful societies through values-based education. Areas of Focus The internship includes: Research into peace education Analysis of educational inequalities Examination of displacement contexts Democratic participation in schools Social cohesion initiatives Internship Opportunity 2: Community Learning Hubs and the Happy Schools Initiative The second internship explores one of the newest components of the Happy Schools Framework—the concept of Community Learning Hubs . UNESCO s recent Working Paper No. 19 established five principles connecting community learning hubs to the Happy Schools Framework. However, UNESCO notes that there is still limited evidence demonstrating how schools actually implement these principles in practice. This internship therefore aims to investigate: How schools operationalize Community Hub principles Which Happy Schools pillars support community engagement Challenges schools encounter when functioning as community hubs Ways multi-service community hubs can implement the Happy Schools Framework Key Research Questions The second internship will explore questions such as: How are Community Hubs implemented in schools using the Happy Schools Framework? Which of the four pillars most effectively support community learning? What barriers prevent schools from functioning as community hubs? How can non-school community hubs adopt the Happy Schools Framework? What Interns Will Gain Participants will benefit from: International research experience Direct collaboration with UNESCO experts Exposure to global education policy Experience conducting applied educational research Professional networking International work experience Practical understanding of education for sustainable development Research skills in education and public policy Why This Internship Matters Education systems worldwide face increasing challenges related to: Conflict Displacement Inequality Mental wellbeing Community resilience Social cohesion The UNESCO Doctoral Internships provide researchers with an opportunity to contribute directly to solutions that improve learning environments for millions of learners globally. By supporting research into Happy Schools, peace education, and community learning, interns become part of UNESCO s broader effort to create equitable, inclusive, and sustainable education systems.
